text:
noah: FYI seeing apiserver 502/503 spike in eu-west2 around 02:03 UTC, lots of etcd follower reconnects and controller-manager restarts. GPU provisioning jobs failing with API errors.

elaine: graphs show BGP route churn from the cloud provider at ~02:02, matches the apiserver outage window. netteam posted a notice about a peering maintenance but said it shouldn't impact control plane.

jord: checked etcd logs: `etcdserver: rejected connection from remote peer x.x.x.x: i/o timeout` then leader transfer. snippet:```2026-02-15T02:03:05Z etcdserver: raft.node: leader changed from 2 to 4; term: 7```

monitor-bot: alert: apiserver_error_rate_high (eu-west2) · etcd_peer_iowait (3 instances) · incident logged INC-2026-559.

noah: interestingly, the control plane frontends are behind the cloud LB which suddenly switched advertised next-hops; some client connections to etcd proxies were blackholed briefly.

tim: I'm seeing kubelet churn on the gpu worker nodes too — nodes briefly report NotReady when API calls time out, then recover. That caused the GPU autoscaler to trigger a small scale-down and immediately re-up, causing extra churn.

elaine: can we fail over control plane traffic to the secondary peering? cloud supports failover but requires reprogramming route announcements — ops do we have a playbook?

ops: we have a peering-failover runbook but it's invasive and increases cross-region egress. recommend mitigating in-cluster first: (1) increase etcd client timeouts from 8s->25s on apiserver sidecars, (2) raise controller-manager leaseRenewDeadline 20s->60s to avoid spurious leader loss, (3) add a short LB healthcheck pause to avoid flapping backends.

jord: rolling those timeouts now in a canary: patched apiserver deployment config and bumped etcd dial timeout in client flags. Running in eu-west2-canary subset.

noah: also, run `ip route get` and verify AS path from LB to control-plane nodes; share logs. quick command: `sudo ip route show table all | grep next-hop`

tim: ran conntrace dump on a worker node, lots of TCP_RST from the LB during the window. suspect asymmetric path during peering change left half-open sockets.

monitor-bot: cluster autoscaler: scaledown cancelled (safety) · added annotation: scale-action-blocked=true.

elaine: short-term mitigation approved: pause autoscaler for the region, pause any non-critical peering changes, and continue canary of timeouts. If canary is healthy for 15m we roll.

noah: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated customers experienced transient provisioning timeouts and one long-running job retried but eventually succeeded. No data loss. I'm drafting a note for SRE->support.

jord: canary results at 02:15 UTC look good: apiserver 5xx back to baseline on canary hosts, leader elections stopped. Scheduling full rollout in 5m.

ops: added follow-ups: (A) add pre-check in peering job to query control-plane health before changing advertised routes, (B) update autoscaler to suppress scale actions during control-plane instability, (C) add eBPF conntrack cleanup in node pre-shutdown hook.

tim: cost note: if we do peering failover or mirror control plane into another region for safety, estimate ~40% infra uplift for standby bandwidth and extra etcd replicas; flagging for finance if we go that route.

elaine: agreed, keep failover as last resort. postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (peering maintenance caused next-hop churn -> asymmetric paths -> TCP resets -> etcd leader jitter), mitigations, and customer impact.

noah: assigning actions: jord -> roll timeouts to eu-west2, ops -> add peering pre-checks, elaine -> incident doc & comms.

monitor-bot: incident status: mitigated · responders assigned (jord, ops, elaine) · priority P2.

noah: update in 10m, closing thread unless alerts reappear. :white_check_mark:
